content.content:
# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). The search form needs its action and placeholder swapped to use dynamic game data instead of hidden inputs, while the loaders, aside, and start sections all become optional HTML blocks that render empty when there's no data.

For the popular and fresh rails, I'm keeping the section markup intact but slotting the inner content and view-all links, treating the whole sections as hideable blocks so empty rails just disappear. Categories and plans get the same whole-section slot treatment, and the FAQ answers become individual text slots keyed to each question.

Then for the final CTA area I'm collapsing the deploy paragraph and button block into a single slot, updating the hero title to use the generic game name placeholder, dropping the hardcoded mods-data script, and doing a careful ordered find-and-replace across the main content so every literal "Minecraft" and its URL path get swapped for the game name and href tokens without clobbering earlier replacements.

Now I'm reworking the JS: swapping the parsed mods JSON and base URL constants for the generic `__NXM` equivalents, making the palette build hrefs from the new URL variable, and replacing the hardcoded "64,709 mods" empty-state message with a dynamic total count label. I'm also updating the essentials script's click handler so the toast/validation logic still works with the new generic structure.

Since the selection state isn't preserved on the dashboard side, I want an honest label instead — something like "3 picked · open my dashboard" — and I'll set that text via the inner span rather than overwriting the whole anchor's children.

For the game hero and plan cards, I'm swapping the marketing use-case copy for real tier specs pulled from GameTier — slots, CPU, disk — and labeling the deploy button with the actual RAM amount, which feels more truthful than fabricated tier names. I still need to work out the per-game loaders/platforms query using Prisma's raw query against the GameMod table, and figure out how price should display alongside these real specs.

For pricing, I'm keeping it simple with the price shown per month, plus a note about the intro rate reverting to the regular price after the intro period. I'm also revising the marketing lede for non-installable game families — since one-click mod install isn't universally true, I'm rewording it to emphasize DDoS protection, daily restore points, and full file access via Files for manual uploads instead.

Now I'm moving on to the JSON-LD structure for each game page: an ItemList for most-downloaded mods plus product schema for hosting plans, along with the auto-generated FAQPage. For metadata I'm crafting a title and description that reflect the live verified mod count, with a tailored version for non-installable games noting downloads happen from each source. Then I'll set the crumb label and start writing the mods-minecraft.ts file.

For 'unsupported', the phrasing is `${Source} marks this mod as not supported on servers. It runs in players' own games, not on your server.` For null, I skip the block and FAQ entirely.

I'm also planning the stats row with up to four fields like downloads, last updated, license, loaders, file size, and source, plus highlight logic for non-curated cards — game versions supported, loaders it runs on, and footprint based on file size or performance impact.

Now I'm adding license, last update, and dependency highlights, taking the first three and showing them if there are at least two, labeled "From source data," with icons cycling through physical/AI/checkmark for additional entries. For the compatibility card, I'm mapping out rows for game, loaders, and server-side requirement status with appropriate styling for required, optional, and other states.

For the "Add" panel, I plan to compute install support server-side using family and source, then get the current user and their eligible servers via a server action imported directly into the server component—reasoning that since the page is already forced dynamic, calling currentUser again here is fine. Writing panel JS...

I've confirmed this is a shared port bug: swap_buttons strips the "au-btn" class that the design's own mobile CSS relies on to hide buttons, and it also affects the hub even though hub doesn't visibly break since its hero isn't a grid layout. I'm considering whether I can fix this within my wire by re-adding the "au-btn" class after swap_buttons runs.

Adding "au-btn" back risks pulling in conflicting aurora styling against the nxm-btn look, so instead I'm leaning toward injecting a scoped `<style>` block directly in the body markup with a media query that hides the button on mobile for my specific pages, while separately flagging the root cause for a shared fix. I still need to verify the grid collapses properly once the button is hidden, and also check the mob-mod-cmp mobile behavior on the mod page.

I'm noticing the 2x2 stats grid clips long values like the license and loader list on mobile, so I'm adding inline wrapping styles to the stat divs and truncating the loaders display to two entries plus a "+N" indicator for the rest.

For the mobile search button, I'm adding a media query that hides the button under 600px, relying on the on-screen keyboard's "Go" key for submission as intended by the design. I also want to hide the mds row entirely when there's only a single stat to show.

## NxLabs pages wired to real data: /mods, /mods/games/[family], /mods/games/[family]/all, /mods/[family]/[slug]

All four slugs now read from the system on every request. The port audit says `wired` with no stale values for all four. `npx tsc --noEmit` passes. I made no commits and no staging deploy.

**Heads-up:** another agent's commit `e4a2fcbe62` ("native page support + legal pages") picked up early in-progress versions of `mods-lib.ts`, `nxlabs.ts`, `mods-minecraft.ts`, `tools/nxm/wire/nxlabs.py` and `mods_minecraft.py`. The final versions of those files, and everything else below, are uncommitted in the worktree.

### Files (only mine)
- **Loaders** in `/root/nxeon-worktrees/marketing-nxm/app/nxm/_data/`:
  - `nxlabs.ts` (hub)
  - `mods-minecraft.ts` (per-game)
  - `mods-minecraft-browse.ts` (browse)
  - `mod-lithium.ts` (mod page)
  - `mods-lib.ts`: shared helpers — ports of the design's card builders (`mods_ui.py` card, hub pick cards), the `mod_tags.py` TAGS/illustrations, family lookup and 404, real game art checks, `db.gamePlan` tiers, links, buttons, ItemList JSON-LD.
- **Wire modules** in `/root/nxeon-worktrees/marketing-nxm/tools/nxm/wire/`: `nxlabs.py`, `mods_minecraft.py`, `mods_minecraft_browse.py`, `mod_lithium.py`. The last three assert that no Minecraft/Lithium/Modrinth/"$" value from the design is left on the page.
- Regenerated with the approved command. New routes: `app/nxm/mods/games/[family]/page.tsx`, `.../all/page.tsx` and `app/nxm/mods/[family]/[slug]/page.tsx`.

### What each page does now
- **Hub (/mods):**
  - All counts come from the catalogue: 22,046 mods, 22 games and 5.9B downloads on the staging DB.
  - Game tiles use real art from `lib/games.ts`; games with no art get a monogram.
  - The "Popular" game chips are the five games with the most real downloads.
  - The sources list comes from the real sources in the catalogue.
  - Editor's picks are the real featured mods. The top-10 ranking and podium are real downloads.
  - "Browse by what you need" is `mod_tags.py` tags aggregated over real categories, each with its top real mods.
  - The drag-to-install demo is stocked with real mods and is labelled "Illustration".
  - **Search:** typing shows quick matches from preloaded real data. Enter sends `?q=` to a real `queryCatalogMods` results section (sort, per-game counts, pagination). With a game chip picked, it redirects to that game's browse page with `?q=`.
- **Per-game (/mods/games/[family]):**
  - Works for every family that `listCatalogFamilies` returns; anything else 404s.
  - Real hero art, count and loaders (from `GameMod.loaders`).
  - "Start here" is the family's featured mods, and is hidden if it has none.
  - The Most downloaded and Recently updated rails are hidden when empty.
  - Category tiles are the family's real categories with its top mods.
  - The upsell uses that family's real `db.gamePlan` tiers ("Most popular" = `GamePlan.featured`) with `deployHref` links, and is hidden when the family has no plans (e.g. cs16).
  - "One-click" wording appears only where installs are actually supported (`lib/mod-install-support.ts`); other families get honest wording.
- **Browse (/mods/games/[family]/all):**
  - Server-side `?q`, `?category` (the family's real categories; an unknown category 404s), `?sort` and `?page`.
  - Real totals and a real pagination window.
  - Sort and category controls navigate to real URLs.
- **Mod page (/mods/[family]/[slug]):**
  - Inactive, unknown or upstream-dead mods 404.
  - Everything shown comes from the mod's real row: icon (falls back to a monogram), author, stats, the source's gallery (hidden when there is none), its long description, compatibility, and verified-at-source details.
  - Highlights: the design's curated set for Lithium only. For every other mod they are built from real fields only (versions, loaders, footprint/impact, dependencies, license, last update), and hidden if fewer than 2 are available.
  - Side-support wording comes from `serverSide`.
  - **Add to a server:**
    - Logged-in visitors see their real eligible servers (`getEligibleServersForMod`) and hand off to the portal's real install flow at `/dashboard/nxlabs/[family]/[slug]`.
    - Anonymous visitors get a login link.
    - Games where install isn't supported show the system's own message.
    - "New server" uses real tiers and live regions, with a per-tier and per-region deploy link.
    - The design's fake "Lithium is live on mc-survival" install animation is removed.
  - External links point to the mod's real source URL.
  - The related rail uses `relatedCatalogMods`.
- **SEO on every page:** title and description from real names and counts, canonical, breadcrumbs, and FAQPage built from each page's own FAQ.
  - Hub: FAQPage plus an ItemList, which matches or exceeds the live `/mods`.
  - Per-game: ItemList plus Product/AggregateOffer from real plans (the live page has neither).
  - Browse: ItemList.
  - Mod: the same SoftwareApplication as the live page (plus url and softwareRequirements; offers omitted for paid mods).
  - Hub and browse pages with a search query are noindex.

### Verified
- Pages checked: Minecraft, Factorio, cs16 (no plans), Rust, Vintage Story; mod pages Lithium, Cobblemon (8-image gallery, lightbox works), SharpTimer and Admin Radar (no icon), BetterRuins, a Garry's Mod workshop mod, Factorio's flib.
- Unknown family, mod, category and upstream-dead mod (valheim/configuration-manager) all return 404.
- XSS attempts in `q` come back escaped; an out-of-range page number clamps to the last page.
- Interactions work: typeahead, chip-to-browse redirect, sort and category navigation, tabs, size/region deploy links, gallery lightbox.
- 1440 and 390 screenshots match the design, with no horizontal overflow.
- Not tested: the "My servers" list for a logged-in user who owns a matching server (the code path is the live page's own).
- Screenshots are in `/tmp/claude-0/-root/ec6fa978-d80b-4147-9982-eea470598e2c/scratchpad/shots/`: `cmp-hub-*`, `cmp-game-*`, `cmp-browse-*`, `cmp-mod-*` (design on the left, ours on the right), `mob-0.png`, `game-390-fixed.png`, `cobble-1440-top.png`, `sharp-1440-top.png`, `hub-search.png`.

### Couldn't be sourced (dropped or reworded)
- **Things the catalogue doesn't have:** no client-side flag (only `serverSide`), no author URL, no GitHub repo URL for Modrinth mods, no "configurable" field. The mod page shows none of these except Lithium's curated text.
- **Minecraft freshness:** staging has no `upstreamUpdatedAt` for Minecraft, so its "Recently updated" rail and "last updated" stat are hidden.
- **"Name A to Z" sort:** there is no name sort, so the browse sort buttons are Most downloaded, Newest in NxLabs (`createdAt`) and Featured first. The "Recently updated" rail's "View all" link therefore opens the Newest sort, which is by date added, not by upstream update.
- **Bulk install:** there is no bulk-install action, so the essentials "Add all" button now opens the dashboard's per-game NxLabs page.

### mod_tags coverage
- The catalogue has one category per mod, in each source's own words. I mapped categories to the 10 tags only where the tag's description is plainly true.
- That covers 3,155 of 22,046 public mods (14.3%). The rest get the neutral default tile, which just states the category name.
- The biggest unmapped categories are workshop (9,521), content, tweaks, items, mods/mod, crafting, cosmetics and map. Covering them needs new illustrations and copy from design (OPEN-ITEMS B).
- `mod_tags.py`'s circuit, boxes, compass, chat and target illustrations fall back to the gear, exactly as the design's own code does.

### Shared changes needed (not made)
1. **Missing-download mods sort first (lib bug, also on the live site).** In `lib/mods-catalog.ts`, sorting by downloads puts mods with no download count first. `queryCatalogMods` "downloads"/"featured" and `relatedCatalogMods` should use `{downloads: {sort: "desc", nulls: "last"}}`. It shows on Minecraft's browse page, which starts with 4 mods that have no downloads, and on the hub's search results.
2. **Sorts:** add `updated` (`upstreamUpdatedAt`) and `name` sorts to `queryCatalogMods` so the design's sort buttons can be honest.
3. **Breadcrumbs:** `crumbs()` is built from the URL path, so mod pages read Home › NxLabs › Mod with no game level, and browse pages for anything but Minecraft skip the game level. Loaders need a way to pass their own trail.
4. **Staging path prefix:** `mods-lib.ts` has its own `NXM_BASE = "/nxm"` copied from nxmlib `BASE`. `lib.ts` should export it so launch is one switch.
5. **Mobile search button:** `swap_buttons` drops the `au-btn` class, so the design's mobile rule hiding the search button stopped matching and the Minecraft page overflowed on phones. I patched this with a small scoped `<style>` in my two wires; a fix in the porter would cover all pages.
6. **Per-game accent colour:** the accent is the design's `#3FD89A` for every game. Per-game colours live in `GAME_VISUAL`, but that sits in a `"use client"` module. It needs moving to a server-safe module plus the override hook you offered.

### Owner decisions
- Should Lithium keep its curated layer (highlights, details, "vanilla stays vanilla", side diagram, requires/config text), labelled "Curated by NxLabs"?
- Should the demo server name "my-server" and the "Illustration" label be kept in the drag-to-install section?
- Illustrations are needed for the high-volume unmapped categories.
- Should families with no hosting plans (cs16, dayz) keep their mods pages? They currently show mods with download links only.

Main here — follow-up. A coverage check of the live sitemap vs /nxm found the live /game-servers/mods page (app/(marketing)/game-servers/mods — the "mod catalogue for game servers" page; per project notes it's honest that there's no universal mod installer and sells file/SFTP access, check the page) has no new-site version. Address this before completing your current task.

Installing a mod by hand

For any game or mod the one-click store doesn’t cover. It’s your server, laid out like a real one.

01

Upload it: file manager or SFTP

Drag the plugin into the in-dashboard file manager, or connect over SFTP with the credentials on every server. Real file access, no ticket.

02

Drop it in the right folder

oxide/plugins, mods/, BepInEx/plugins, addons/: wherever your game’s modding platform expects it.

03

Restart from the console

Hit restart in the panel or reload from the live console. The mod loads and it’s live. Snapshot a backup first if you’re experimenting.

{{nxm:popular:html}}

Nothing artificially blocked

The same access you’d have on hardware in your closet, minus the hardware.

No mod limits

No mod-count cap, no plugin allow-list, no “contact support to enable file access.” If the game supports it, your server can run it.

Real SFTP access

Full SFTP straight into your own server and a file manager in the dashboard.

Backup before you experiment

Snapshot your world before installing anything untested, and roll it straight back if a mod breaks something.

Live console and RCON

Tail logs and send commands from the panel, without a second tool.

Mod support, answered

What you can install, and how.

Is this a one-click mod installer?

{{nxm:faq.oneclick}}

Can I install any mod I want?

Yes. Nxeon doesn’t curate, block or limit mods. You get full file and console access, so anything your game’s modding platform (Oxide, Forge, BepInEx, Steam Workshop and so on) supports, you can install.

Is there a limit on how many mods I can run?

No artificial limit from us. The practical ceiling is your plan’s RAM, CPU and storage: a heavier modpack just needs a larger tier.

What about Steam Workshop mods?

{{nxm:faq.workshop}}

A mod broke my world. What now?

Roll back to a backup taken before you installed it. We recommend snapshotting first any time you try something untested.

Your server, modded your way.

{{nxm:final.sub}}

{{nxm:final.ctas:html}}
{{FOOTER}}

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. # Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.

- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

## Follow-up: /nxm/game-servers/mods is built and returns 200

This is a native page in the NxLabs design language, and every value on it comes from the system at request time. The port audit shows `game-servers-mods  wired`. Typecheck passes for my files; the only tsc errors are in `app/nxm/_data/use-case.ts` (`stack` and `someCards` not found), which is another agent's file. It renders at 1440 and 390 with no horizontal overflow and no page errors. I made no commits and no deploys.

### Files
- **Native page:** `/root/nxeon-worktrees/marketing-nxm/tools/nxm/native/game-servers-mods/`
  - `body.html` holds the markup with slots only.
  - `page.css` is the design package's NxLabs styles copied verbatim (`nxlabs/page.css` + `_modsgame.css` + `_modscards.css`), plus a small per-game table style for this page.
  - `page.js` does the hero poster rows, the game filter and the carousels.
  - `meta.json`.
- **Wire:** `tools/nxm/wire/game_servers_mods.py`
- **Loader:** `app/nxm/_data/game-servers-mods.ts` (reuses `mods-lib.ts`)
- **Shared lines (my slug only):**
  - `ROUTES` in `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py`: `"game-servers-mods": "/game-servers/mods"`
  - `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`: one `/game-servers/mods` entry (live title, crumb "Mod support")
- **Generated:** `app/nxm/game-servers/mods/page.tsx` and `app/nxm/_pages/game-servers-mods/*`

### What is on the page
The live page's honest framing is kept: one-click installs only where NxLabs can really place mods, and full SFTP, file manager and console access on every game.

- **Hero:** real counts (22,046 mods on staging; production will show its own 64,709), the number of one-click games, and the number of hosted games.
- **One-click list:** derived from `lib/mod-install-support.ts`, checked per game *and* per source.
  - On staging this gives Minecraft, Rust and Valheim.
  - Rust shows 29 of its 30 mods as one-click, because Codefling is not a supported download source.
  - Steam Workshop one-click is labelled as such.
- **"Mod support, game by game" table:** one row for each of the 42 games with an active game plan, and it can be filtered.
  - Each row has the real NxLabs mod count, how mods install, the "from" price from the game's cheapest real plan, and deploy links built with `deployHref`.
  - It links to the game's `/nxm/mods/games/<family>` page when the game has mods, and to the staged `/<game>-server-hosting` page when one exists.
  - 11 games (ARK, DST, Unturned, Project Zomboid, TF2 and others) support one-click installs but have no mods listed on staging. Those rows say exactly that instead of claiming one-click.
- **"What servers are running" rail:** the real top-downloaded mods across all games.
- **Copy kept from the live page:** the manual-install steps, the trust points and the FAQ. The FAQ answers about one-click and Steam Workshop now name the real games instead of a hardcoded list.

### SEO and JSON-LD (matches or exceeds the live page)
- Title is the live one. The description names the real one-click games.
- Canonical is `/game-servers/mods`.
- Breadcrumb is Home › Game servers › Mod support.
- JSON-LD:
  - FAQPage built from the page's own 5 questions.
  - Product/AggregateOffer from real plans: 42 offers, low price $2.99. The live page has 5 hand-typed prices.
  - ItemList of the top mods.

### For the owner
- The live page's hardcoded claim "one-click Mod Store for Minecraft, Rust, and Valheim" matches staging's catalogue today. It will drift as Steam Workshop titles get NxLabs listings; the new page follows the system automatically.
- Screenshots are in `/tmp/claude-0/-root/ec6fa978-d80b-4147-9982-eea470598e2c/scratchpad/shots/`: `gsm-a.png` and `gsm-b.png` (1440), `gsm-m.png` (390).

The coordinator sent a message while you were working:
Main here — owner feedback on the NxLabs pages:
1) /nxm/mods hero: the search results dropdown is clipped by the hero (overflow). Make the typeahead panel float above the following sections (portal it or fix the hero's overflow/z-index/stacking) at 1440 and 390.
2) "Where are the mod images/logos on the mods pages?" — cards (featured/editor's picks, rails, category tiles, related, browse grid) currently lead with the design's generic tag illustrations as the banner, with the real icon small. Lead with the mod's OWN imagery: first image from GameMod.galleryUrls (real screenshots/banners from the source) as the card banner (lazy-loaded, object-fit cover, sized sensibly — Modrinth/other CDN URLs are fine or proxy through the app's image optimizer if the CSP requires), plus the real icon prominently; only mods with no gallery fall back to the tag illustration (and ones with no icon to the monogram). Same on the mod detail page hero (gallery lead image as the hero art when present). Check the CSP img-src allows the CDNs (img-src includes https:), and handle broken images (onerror → fallback).
3) "Are all the mods actually organized in categories or is that section just for show?" — today GameMod.category is one free-text category per mod in each source's own words (e.g. 9.5k 'workshop') and the hub's "Browse by what you need" maps only ~14% to the 10 design tags. Build a real taxonomy: a normalized category map (~12–16 clear categories, e.g. Performance, World & generation, Gameplay, Admin & permissions, Economy, Maps, Weapons & items, Vehicles, UI & HUD, Library/API, Cosmetics, Quality of life, Protection & anti-cheat…) derived from each mod's source category + its tags/description keywords where the source category is generic ('workshop', 'mod', 'content'), in a shared module (e.g. lib/nxlabs-taxonomy.ts or app/nxm/_data/mods-taxonomy.ts — computed at query time, no DB writes), used by the hub's category section, per-game category tiles, browse ?category filter, and mod pages. Report the resulting coverage (% of public mods in a real category, not "Other") on staging, and give each category an illustration (reuse/extend the design's mod_tags illustrations).
Everything stays real (no invented counts). Same rules as before: only your files + your slugs' ROUTES/registry lines; no commits/deploys; one browser at a time; disk is watched. Report files, coverage numbers, screenshots.

Address this before completing your current task.

content.thinking:
This is a substantial task, so I'm mapping it out. I'm looking at why the typeahead is getting clipped—the row container has overflow hidden which cuts off the dropdown, so I need to adjust the CSS so the outer element allows overflow while the inner rows keep their own clipping for scrolling.

I also realize card banners need gallery images pulled in, but ModSummary doesn't currently include galleryUrls, so I need a helper that batch-fetches gallery images for a list of mod IDs and attaches a banner field to each summary before rendering the cards.

For category tiles, I'm thinking they could show a faded background image from a top example mod's gallery, or simpler, just a small row of icons from a few example mods within the tile.

For the mod detail hero, I want to replace the placeholder SVG art with the actual gallery image when available, wrapping it so the slot can swap in an image with an overlay shade instead of the default vector art.

Now I'm outlining the taxonomy data module with roughly 14 categories like Performance and others still to define.

I'm also considering folding mod-packs and total conversions into their own "Modpacks & overhauls" bucket, keeping the total category count around 16-18. For assignment logic, I'd first normalize by mapping raw source categories to my taxonomy keys, then fall back to keyword matching in the name and description for generic categories like 'other' or 'misc'. The trickier part is that browse filtering by category needs to work against computed taxonomy categories rather than raw DB categories, so filtering would need to match either mods whose raw category maps directly to that taxonomy key, or generic-category mods whose descriptions match the relevant keywords.

I need to make sure that if a generic mod's description matches keywords for multiple taxonomy categories, it only gets counted under the highest-priority match by excluding earlier-priority keyword matches -- doable but adds complexity to the query, and I'll need to query db.gameMod directly rather than relying solely on the existing catalog helper since this taxonomy filtering is computed on the fly per the coordinator's request.

Actually, I'm reconsidering: instead of building exclusion logic to keep categories mutually exclusive, I could let keyword-matched mods belong to multiple categories, which is fine for browsing/filtering purposes even though it means category coverage percentages could sum past 100% -- the mod's own page would still show a single primary category regardless.

For computing per-family counts consistently, I'm thinking of writing a raw SQL query with a CASE expression that mirrors the same classification rules used in TypeScript, so a single GROUP BY query gives exact parity with the app logic.

Simplifying: rather than tracking a separate generic set, any category not directly mapped falls through to keyword matching against name and description, and if nothing matches it lands in "other." That handles odd unmapped categories like "Furry" or "Meme" the same way, so the ruleset becomes cleaner — just a direct map plus ordered keyword rules.

Since raw substring matching risks false positives on short words, I need word-boundary regex matching in Postgres, which means using raw SQL queries rather than Prisma's built-in filtering. I'll write a raw query that selects matching mod IDs using the classification expression with parameterized regex patterns, get the total count, then fetch the full rows via Prisma's findMany while preserving the original ordering.

Running ~17 regex rules across up to 64k rows per hub page load could be slow (maybe 0.5-1s), so I should cache the counts with unstable_cache for 600 seconds, similar to the existing pattern. For per-family browse queries the row count is smaller and manageable. I also need to make sure the JS-side classification logic used for mod cards stays consistent with the SQL regex boundaries, or better, just classify consistently in one place so displayed categories match the taxonomy labels rather than raw values.

Mod page tag tiles should show the taxonomy category with an illustration, and card labels could reuse the same taxonomy label for consistency. Since Postgres's \m/\M word boundaries behave essentially the same as JS's \b (both treat alnum+underscore as word characters), I can safely build a single combined regex per rule and reuse the same pattern shape in both places, just need to coalesce null descriptions to empty strings. I'm also thinking about false positives, like "map" matching inside "minimap" — word boundaries should prevent that from being an issue.

Rule ordering matters since specific terms should be checked before generic ones, so I'm planning a two-pass approach: check all rules against the name first, then fall back to checking against the description. I'll limit the description scan to the first 300-400 characters to reduce cost and noise, applying that same truncation in both SQL and JS. Now I'm drafting the actual category/keyword lists, starting with "Libraries & APIs" and noting that some mods like Fabric API or ViaVersion/Geyser might better fit under a "Compatibility" category instead.

I'm merging libraries and compatibility into one bucket with keywords like library, api, framework, dependency, patch, and compat, while deciding that translation/localization terms should go under a smaller "Quality of life" or language-specific grouping instead. Next I'm building out keyword sets for performance (fps, lag, tps, optimization) and starting on the admin/moderation category.

For admin, I'm noting things like "Serverside Only" are just flags rather than categories, so those stay as keywords rather than a top-level bucket, and I add ban/kick/permission terms there. Then I sketch protection/anti-cheat (grief, claim, anticheat, distinguishing from Vintage Story's unrelated "Cheat" mods), economy (shop, currency, trade, market), and world generation (biome, terrain, structure, ruins).

For maps, I'm adding dungeon/village/cave terms, then realizing many Gmod addons are literally maps identifiable by name prefixes like gm_, ttt_, rp_, de_, cs_, surf_, so I plan a regex pattern matching those prefixes to auto-tag them as maps.

Then for the "Weapons, items & crafting" category, I'm listing keywords covering weapons, armor, tools, crafting, recipes, sweps, and ammo, folding crafting-related items into this bucket rather than gameplay.

Next I'm working out remaining categories: vehicles & ships with keywords like car, boat, plane, helicopter, tank, mech, train, drone; UI & HUD with terms like hud, interface, menu, minimap, tooltip; and cosmetics & visuals possibly merged with audio, covering skins, textures, shaders, playermodels, and sound/music.

I'm also defining a "quality of life" category with keywords like qol, tweaks, utility, convenience, auto-sort, and stacking, while being careful that broad terms like "auto" don't over-match.

Next I'm mapping out "social" for chat/discord/community terms, "mobs" for creatures and NPCs like animals, zombies, bosses, and pets, and starting on "tech" for automation-related keywords like machine, conveyor, power, generator, and reactor.

Overhauls & modpacks" covers total conversions, difficulty rebalancing, and realism/hardcore tweaks. Then thinking about "gameplay" as a category—content is tricky since it's generic in Factorio terms, but genuinely new content additions probably map here anyway, so I need to decide how to treat that fallback case.

I'll settle on: check the direct specific map first, then keywords, then a fallback for semi-generic terms (content maps to gameplay, while mod/mods/workshop/other/misc fall to "other"). That gets me down from 19 categories to something closer to the coordinator's suggested 12-16 by merging building into gameplay-overhauls, ui into quality-of-life, and protection into admin — landing at 16 clean categories: library, performance, admin, economy, worldgen, maps, items, vehicles, cosmetics, qol, social, mobs, tech, minigames, building, gameplay.

Now for illustrations, I want each category tile to reuse or extend the existing mod_tags CSS-animated shapes where possible, and since I can't add new page CSS, I'll extend coverage with inline SVG illustrations inside the tile containers instead. I'm mapping out per-category assets — label, description, tile illustration kind, and card SVG — deciding which categories get existing shapes versus custom inline SVG.

I also need to plan taxonomy-driven counts for hub categories with cross-game examples, extend browse chips and hub queries to accept a category filter, and make mod pages and cards surface the taxonomy label alongside the raw source category for transparency.

For sorting, I'm handling downloads/latest/featured consistently with nulls placed last, and falling back to my taxonomy query only when a category filter is active, otherwise reusing the existing catalog query. Writing classification SQL...

Adding filters for family and search terms, then ordering by downloads with nulls last and pagination. After fetching matching ids I need to map full rows to ModSummary objects, including gallery URLs for banners, and write a separate helper to fetch banner images for list-based queries that don't already have full rows.

For classifying mod categories on cards, I need matching keyword rules that work identically in JS and SQL—using word-boundary regex in JS (`\b`) and Postgres's equivalent (`\m`/`\M`), including a special pattern for map-name prefixes like `gm_`, `ttt_`, `rp_` combined with the alternation of category keywords.

I also need to handle multi-word and hyphenated terms correctly, compute actual coverage percentages instead of lumping things into "other," and make sure category keys work cleanly as URL slugs. For the hub page showing top examples per category, I'm weighing whether running eight separate top-3 queries against ~45k rows is too slow, and considering caching the whole category block instead.

Actually, a cleaner solution is to use a single SQL query with a window function to rank mods by downloads within each category and grab the top 3 per category in one pass, then cache that with unstable_cache keyed by family. I'll also add small icon rows for the top mods on each category tile, then move on to writing mods-taxonomy.ts.

content.thinking: I'm tracing the CSS override causing the gap — that background-size rule from the stylesheet applies at all widths, so at wide/short aspect ratios the scaled image doesn't fill the container. Overriding with cover would fix the gap but might disrupt the designer's intended crop at normal sizes, so I'm weighing a background-size:max alternative instead. I realize the gap only happens when the viewport is wider relative to the image height than the zoom factor allows, so instead of fighting with background-size math, I should just swap to an actual `` element positioned absolutely with `object-fit: cover` and a tall height plus bottom anchoring — that guarantees full bleed while preserving the bottom-weighted crop. Checking the other hero sections, most already use full-bleed techniques (rotated insets, gradient insets, SVG slice), so this dark-strip gap issue seems isolated to this one hero art component. I'm now also noticing the `.pal-res` positioning rules live outside any media query in the page stylesheet, which seems worth investigating further. Actually, tracing this further — the top-level `.pal` flex column ordering makes `.pal-res` static within flow, so it likely grows the hero's height rather than getting clipped by overflow, which contradicts the reported symptom unless the container has a fixed height constraint I'm missing. I should just test this directly in the browser by opening the hub palette and taking a screenshot to see what's actually happening.

I see the absolute-positioned element's bottom edge exceeds the hero's bottom, so it's getting clipped by overflow:hidden. On the 390px viewport the results show zero items, so I suspect the search results are hidden or the input isn't registering the typed text properly on mobile.

For the fix, I'll wrap each section's background layers (rows/shade/art) in a dedicated clipping container set to absolute positioning with overflow hidden and negative z-index, then change the parent section itself to overflow:visible with a positive z-index so it stacks correctly above later sections. I'll apply this same wrapping pattern to both the nlh and mgh sections. Then I need to check the pal component's filtering logic to figure out why it's rendering zero items on mobile.

I'll test again after the fix with a screenshot to confirm items display properly, then move on to building the taxonomy module.

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.

HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

That POST with RSC headers is likely a server action triggered by some client component, causing an RSC re-render of the page. This would explain the shorter length after — React compares the new dangerouslySetInnerHTML string against the previous prop value, not against actual DOM state, so any inline changes made directly to the DOM get wiped out when the new HTML string is applied.

I'm trying to figure out what would make the server-rendered string differ between two renders of the same page. Things like mod ordering and the "ago" timestamp calculation seem deterministic enough not to change within seconds, so I'm now suspecting the real culprit is client-side DOM mutations (like the nav's inline top position) that React can't see happening, meaning it may just be reapplying the same string and stomping on runtime changes regardless of whether the server output actually changed.

Since this same failure shows up across pages like /nxm/vps too, it's clearly a shared issue — probably a server action (analytics or some provider) triggering a router refresh that re-renders NxmPage and wipes out any listeners or DOM state set after initial load. content.thinking:
The remaining 0.1% of mismatches trace to how Postgres and JS handle word boundaries differently for CJK characters—Postgres treats them as word characters while JS's \b doesn't, causing edge-case matches. I'm considering adjusting the JS regex to use Unicode-aware lookarounds so it treats CJK letters as word characters too, aligning the behavior.

More pressing is performance: full classification takes 2.6s for 22k rows locally, which could balloon to ~7s on production's 64k rows, and the per-family count queries compound this badly on pages like the vehicles hub. The regex-based description matching is clearly the bottleneck, so I'm thinking through caching strategies—precomputing a classification map (id, family, key, downloads, etc.) for all public mods once and reusing it, then doing key/family filtering in JS rather than SQL, while still relying on SQL ILIKE for text search since large ID lists in a WHERE IN clause won't scale well.

I'm leaning toward wrapping this computation in an unstable_cache-backed index function, accepting a ~7s cost on cache expiry since Next's stale-while-revalidate behavior means users get stale data instantly while it refreshes in the background. From that index I can derive category counts, top-per-category rankings, and other filtered views without re-running the expensive SQL each time.

For queries with a category key plus a search term, I'd filter the index by key first, then run a single SQL lookup to find which candidate ids actually match the search string, intersect the sets, and sort/paginate in JS. For queries without a key, I'd fall back to the plain SQL path minus the classification logic. I also want to collapse the 22 separate per-family count queries into one combined query grouped by gameFamily when there's a search term, which should be much more efficient. Now I'm sizing out how large that index would be at 64k rows to make sure it's reasonable to cache.

Estimating at roughly 80 bytes per row across six fields, the index comes to about 5MB, which worries me since Next's fetch cache silently refuses anything over 2MB -- though I'm not certain that same limit applies to unstable_cache. Given the uncertainty, I think it's safer to just use a simple in-memory module-level cache with a TTL instead, and trim the index down by dropping unnecessary fields like name to keep only what's essential: id, family, key, downloads, createdAt, and featured status.

Now I'm sketching out the actual implementation: a module-scoped cache holding rows with a timestamp, refreshing every ten minutes, serving stale data while a background refresh happens if needed, and building the query to pull those core fields plus name for sorting purposes.
