input.message: ## Owner feedback on the NxLabs pages: all four items done, plus one shared bug found All four items are fixed on :3033. All 5 of my slugs report `wired` in the port audit. `tsc` is clean for my files (earlier the only errors were in another agent's `use-case.ts`). No page has horizontal overflow at 390 or 1440. I made no commits or deploys. **The bug:** about 3 seconds after every /nxm page loads, the page script's work is thrown away. It looks like the promo popup's server action (`getPromoPopupState`) refreshes the page, and the body is rebuilt from the server. I could only fix it partly on my side; details in "Shared bug" below. ### 1. Search dropdown clipped by the hero (fixed) - **Cause:** the hero section (`.nlh` on /mods, `.mgh` on the per-game page) had `overflow:hidden`, so the absolutely positioned results panel was cut off. - **Fix, in my wires only:** the hero's background layers (poster rows and shade, or the game art and shade) now sit in their own clipping layer. The hero itself gets `overflow:visible;z-index:6`, so the panel floats above the following sections. - **Measured:** the panel now ends at 1116px while the hero ends at 878px (/mods 1440); 1211 vs 987 (/mods 390); 1060 vs 856 (per-game 1440). All 7 results are visible. Screenshot: `shots/pal-cmp.png`. ### 1b. Per-game hero art cut off on the left (fixed) - **Cause:** the design's later `.mgh-art{background-size:auto 138%}` rule sizes the art by height only. On wide screens the image ends up narrower than the viewport, which left a strip on the left. - **Fix:** the art is now a real `` sized 100% wide by 138% tall with `object-fit:cover` and `object-position:70% 100%`. That keeps the design's crop but always fills the full width. The readable-gradient overlay is unchanged. - **Measured at 390, 1280, 1440, 1920 and 2560:** the per-game art spans from x=-51 to 2611 at 2560, i.e. past both edges. The hub, browse and mod heroes already covered the full width (hub rows -671 to 3231; browse and mod 0 to the viewport width), so they don't have the bug. - Screenshot: `shots/bleed-2560.png`. ### 2. The mods' own images - **Cards** (featured picks, rails, related, browse grid, search results, the /game-servers/mods rail) now use the mod's first real `GameMod.galleryUrls` image as the banner. It is lazy-loaded with `object-fit:cover`. If an image fails to load it removes itself, and the category illustration shows through. - **Icons:** the real icon is bigger (48px on rails and browse, 52px on picks). A missing or broken icon falls back to the monogram. - **Category tiles** show the icons of their top 3 real mods. - **Mod page hero** uses the mod's first gallery screenshot when it has one (e.g. Cobblemon); otherwise it keeps the design's category-coloured art. - **Loading the images:** `ModSummary` has no gallery field, so a `withBanners()` batch query adds it. - **Images load fine under the CSP:** its `img-src` includes `https:`. Checked with Modrinth, Vintage Story ModDB, Factorio and Steam CDN images. - **Staging limit:** only sources that publish galleries have banners. Steam Workshop rows in staging have none, so those cards keep the illustration. ### 3. A real taxonomy The new module is `app/nxm/_data/mods-taxonomy.ts`. It has 16 categories: | | | | | |---|---|---|---| | Performance | Libraries & compatibility | Admin & protection | Economy & shops | | World generation | Maps & scenarios | Weapons, items & crafting | Vehicles & ships | | Cosmetics, visuals & audio | Quality of life & UI | Chat & community | Creatures & NPCs | | Technology & automation | Game modes & minigames | Building & decoration | Gameplay & overhauls | - **How a mod is classified:** 1. Its source category, when that already says what the mod is (about 170 source categories are mapped). 2. Otherwise, whole-word keywords in the mod's name, then in the first 400 characters of its description, most specific rules first. 3. Otherwise a small fallback for broad buckets (content/mod/addon count as "Gameplay & overhauls"); anything left is "Other". - **Consistency:** the same rules run in SQL (a CASE with Postgres word-boundary regex) and in JS (Unicode-aware). A full comparison over all 22,046 rows found 0 mismatches. Nothing is written to the database. - **Speed:** classifying the whole catalogue takes about 2.3s on staging. So the result (id, game, category and sort keys) is kept in memory per server process and refreshed in the background after 10 minutes. Counts, top mods per category, filters and per-game match counts all read from it; searches still run in SQL. - **Where it's used:** - Hub "Browse by what you need": all 16 categories, 8 largest shown with real counts, top-3 mods with icons, linking to `/mods?cat=#results`. - Hub search results accept `?cat=`; an unknown value returns 404, and the page is noindex. - Per-game category tiles link to `/all?category=`. - The browse `?category=` chips show each game's categories with real counts; an unknown or empty category returns 404. - Card labels show the new category name. - The mod page's "What kind of mod it is" tile shows the category with its illustration and "Listed on {source} as '{raw category}'", so the source's own word is still visible. - **Illustrations:** each category has one. The design's animated tick/nodes/terrain/path/gear pieces are reused. I added 10 new card illustrations in the design's white-line style: shield, coin, pin, blade, car, brush, chat, paw, circuit, cube. Tile icons are now drawn on the server (see the shared bug below). - **Side fix:** all my lists now sort mods without a download count last. `queryCatalogMods` puts them first; that shared-library issue is still open. **Coverage on staging:** 91.1% of public mods (20,082 of 22,046) land in a real category, up from about 14% with the old tag mapping. | Category | Mods | |---|---| | Quality of life & UI | 4,031 | | Weapons, items & crafting | 3,788 | | Gameplay & overhauls | 2,172 | | Maps & scenarios | 1,838 | | Technology & automation | 1,355 | | Vehicles & ships | 1,153 | | Cosmetics, visuals & audio | 1,097 | | Creatures & NPCs | 888 | | Game modes & minigames | 875 | | Libraries & compatibility | 793 | | World generation | 719 | | Building & decoration | 615 | | Admin & protection | 239 | | Chat & community | 222 | | Economy & shops | 154 | | Performance | 143 | | Other | 1,964 | - **Per game:** 100% for minecraft, rust, valheim, palworld, factorio, sandstorm, eco, cs16 and sunkenland. vintagestory 98%, corekeeper 98%, mordhau 96%, spaceengineers 94%, kf2 92%, cs2 91%, gmod 85%, conan 78%, terraria, necesse and dayz 76%, stationeers 74%, barotrauma 69%. - **What's left in Other:** 1,858 of the 1,964 are Steam Workshop items whose name and description match none of the keywords (many are in Chinese, or are joke/skin items). Improving those needs Workshop tags, which the catalogue doesn't store. ### Shared bug (not in my files; please route) About 3 seconds after any /nxm page loads, a POST to the page's own URL fires. It carries server action `002742…`, which resolves to `getPromoPopupState` in `lib/actions-promo-trial.ts`. The page is then re-rendered from the server and NxmPage's `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` body is rewritten. Everything the page script did is thrown away: typeahead and filter listeners, hero poster rows, Aurora `data-au-icon` icons, nav offsets. The page stays marked as mounted, so the script never runs again. I reproduced it on /nxm/mods and on /nxm/vps. On /nxm/mods, typing in the search after the refresh gives no dropdown. My workaround: my category tile icons are now drawn on the server, so they survive the rewrite. The real fix belongs in NxmPage/PageRuntime: set the body once on the client and ignore re-renders, or re-run the page script after a rewrite. The promo action also shouldn't refresh the page. The site-wide promo overlay (`.marketing-promo-stack`) also intercepts clicks on the hero search; I hid it only in my test screenshots. ### Files (mine only) - New: `app/nxm/_data/mods-taxonomy.ts` - Updated: `app/nxm/_data/{mods-lib,nxlabs,mods-minecraft,mods-minecraft-browse,mod-lithium,game-servers-mods}.ts` - Updated wires: `tools/nxm/wire/{nxlabs,mods_minecraft,mod_lithium}.py` - All five slugs regenerated. ### Screenshots All in `/tmp/claude-0/-root/ec6fa978-d80b-4147-9982-eea470598e2c/scratchpad/shots/`: - `pal-cmp.png`: search dropdown at 1440 and 390 - `bleed-2560.png`, plus the per-game hero at 390 and 1920 in `bleed_nxm_mods_games_minecraft-{390,1920}.png` - `c-hub.png`: picks with gallery banners - `c-hubcats.png`: hub categories with icons - `c-game.png`: Minecraft rails and category tiles - `c-gmod.png`: Garry's Mod categories - `c-vs.png`: Vintage Story browse filtered to World generation - `c-cobble.png`: mod hero with its gallery lead image - `c-prop.png`: Workshop mod category tile - Full pages: `fp-*.png`

content.text:
All four owner items are fixed on staging (:3033), and the full report has gone to the coordinator. Along the way I found a shared bug outside my files that stops page interactivity about 3 seconds after every /nxm page loads.

**The shared bug:** about 3 seconds after load, the promo popup calls a server action (`getPromoPopupState`), which appears to refresh the page from the server. The page body is rebuilt and everything the page script set up is lost: search dropdown, filters, poster rows, icons. The script never runs again. I reproduced it on /nxm/mods and /nxm/vps; on /nxm/mods the search gives no results after the refresh. I made my category icons render on the server so they survive it, but the real fix belongs in the shared page components.

1. **Search dropdown clipped:** fixed. The results panel now floats over the next section at 1440 and 390 on both /mods and the per-game page.
2. **Per-game hero art cut off on the left:** fixed. At wide widths the art was narrower than the screen. It now fills the full width at every size I checked (390, 1280, 1440, 1920, 2560). The /mods, browse and mod-page heroes didn't have this bug.
3. **Mod images:**
   - **Cards:** they now lead with each mod's first real screenshot and a larger real icon. Mods without a screenshot keep the category illustration, and broken images fall back.
   - **Mod pages:** the hero uses the lead screenshot when the mod has one.
   - **Staging gap:** Steam Workshop mods on staging have no screenshots, so their cards still show the illustration.
4. **Categories:** there are now 16 clear categories, worked out from each mod's source category, then keywords in its name and description.
   - **Coverage:** 91.1% of staging's 22,046 public mods land in a real category, up from about 14% before.
   - **Other:** 1,964 are left, and 1,858 of those are Steam Workshop items that no keyword matches. Improving that needs Workshop tags, which the catalogue doesn't store.
   - **Where it's used:** the hub's category section, the per-game category tiles, the browse filter and the mod pages, each category with its own illustration.

I made no commits or deploys.

Files are in `/root/nxeon-worktrees/marketing-nxm`:
- `app/nxm/_data/mods-taxonomy.ts` (new)
